QF.id: VIII Introduction to Clearing and Settlement System_3

question.text: NSE's clearing corporation for equity derivatives is:

explanation.text: The Logic: NSE Clearing Limited (NCL) — formerly National Securities Clearing Corporation Limited (NSCCL) — is the clearing corporation that acts as the central counterparty (CCP) for trades on the National Stock Exchange, including the equity derivatives segment. By novation, NCL becomes the buyer to every seller and the seller to every buyer on NSE, guaranteeing settlement. The Trap: Indian Clearing Corporation Limited (ICCL) is the BSE-group clearing corporation, not NSE's. Clearing Corporation of India Limited (CCIL) handles money-market, government-securities and forex clearing. NSDL is a depository (securities custody), not a clearing corporation. These four entities are commonly confused in derivatives questions. Note: The cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook describes the generic role of the clearing corporation and interoperability, but the pages checked do not specifically name NSE Clearing Limited / NSCCL as the answer. The identification above is general Indian market-infrastructure knowledge, drawn from exchange/regulator public disclosures.
